4
# Guards no production path reaches.
#
# Every `pub fn` named check/verify/validate/require/enforce/assert/reject/
# refuse/deny/guard is a refusal by its own naming. Four of them are
# reachable only from tests, which means they protect the tests.
#
# The number may only go down. Wiring one up, or moving it into a module that
# honestly declares `WIRING: unwired`, lowers it; lower this file in the same
# pull request or the gain is given back silently.
#
# Not a hard zero on purpose. Some of what remains should not be wired at all:
# `verify_answer_challenge_zk_proof` returns `Err` unconditionally on purpose,
# because a Merkle proof not bound to its deal and challenge context is
# replayable across storage deals and networks, and callers are meant to use
# `answer_challenge`, which rebuilds that context from registry state. Calling
# it would satisfy this gate and weaken the chain. A number that can only fall
# gets paid down; a number driven to zero by wiring refusals that exist to
# stay unwired is worse than the number it replaced.
#
# The four, and why each one is still here rather than wired:
#
#   src/ai/execution/verify.rs   verify_execution_proof_structural
#   src/lubot/verify.rs          verify_inference_stark
#       All three verify a STARK over an execution trace, and all three are
#       blocked on the same gate: `MainnetActivation` ships with
#       `verify_merkle_enabled: false` and `verify_inference_enabled: false`,
#       pending external audit of the zkVM opcodes. Wiring them before that
#       audit would put an unaudited proof system on the acceptance path,
#       which is the opposite of what the gate is for. They move when the
#       audit lands, not before.
#
#   src/cross_domain/evm/adapter.rs  verify_deposit
#       The richer sibling of `verify_receipt_proof`: it takes a full relayer
#       proof package (header chain, MPT nodes, receipt) where the wired path
#       takes a receipt proof alone. The module's own safety invariant is that
#       the on-chain verifier never touches the network, so wiring this one
#       means first deciding who assembles the package and how its freshness
#       is bounded. That is a bridge-design question, not a call site.
#
#   src/domain/storage_deal.rs   verify_answer_challenge_zk_proof
#       Returns `Err` unconditionally, on purpose. A Merkle proof not bound to
#       its deal and challenge context is replayable across storage deals and
#       networks; callers are meant to use `answer_challenge`, which rebuilds
#       that context from registry state. Calling this would satisfy the gate
#       and weaken the chain.
#
# Two call sites closed since this file was last written, and the number is
# still five because the five listed below are different guards.
#
#   src/storage/qr_reemit.rs   verify_stream_id
#       Called by `RevealSession::open` against a fold recomputed from the
#       emitted frames. It left the count when that call landed: this gate
#       measures call sites, so wiring removes a guard immediately. What it
#       does not measure is whether the calling module is itself entered by a
#       binary, and `RevealSession` is only re-exported from
#       `src/storage/mod.rs`. That question is written here rather than hidden
#       in the number.
#
#   src/storage/transformed.rs   verify_hash
#       Called by `three_pipe::encode_plain` before the body moves into the A1
#       pack, refusing a payload whose bytes no longer match the digest the
#       transform pinned. Same accounting.
#
# The stale declarations were deleted rather than kept. A `WIRING: unwired` note
# that contradicts the caller graph is worse than no note: it tells the next
# reader not to look.
#
#   src/lubot/mod.rs             validate_inference_grant
#       Wired into `build_lubot_request`, which now takes the grant as a
#       required argument. Two doc comments already claimed the check was
#       performed; nothing performed it.
#
#   src/core/block.rs            verify_signature_with_pubkey
#       Wired into the PoA validation path, which was doing the same two
#       checks inline and could have drifted from them.
#
#   src/budlumxyz/mod.rs         verify_app
#       Deleted. A back-compat alias for `attest_app_as_developer`, named as
#       though it were a third-party audit when it only records a developer's
#       own claim. The production path always called the honest name.
